`friendlyspots` computes similarity between spatial transcriptomics samples based on which labels (e.g. cell types) border one another. Available for R and Python. `friendlyspots` is only compatible with original (non-HD) Visium. ## Installation ::: {.panel-tabset group="language"} ## R ```r remotes::install_github("george-hall-ucl/friendlyspots", subdir = "R") ``` Requires only base R. ## Python ```bash pip install "git+https://github.com/george-hall-ucl/friendlyspots#subdirectory=python" ``` Requires `pandas` and `numpy`. ::: ## Usage Give `spatial_similarity()` one data frame per sample, with columns for `array_row`, `array_col` and `label`: ::: {.panel-tabset group="language"} ## R ```r library(friendlyspots) samples <- list(sample_1 = df1, sample_2 = df2, sample_3 = df3) sim <- spatial_similarity(samples) ``` ## Python ```python from friendlyspots import spatial_similarity samples = {"sample_1": df1, "sample_2": df2, "sample_3": df3} sim = spatial_similarity(samples) ``` ::: This returns a sample × sample matrix of similarity scores: 1 = identical, 0 = least similar pair. See the [example](#example) below and the [Reference](reference.qmd) for all options. ## Example This example uses four mouse brain sections from 10x Genomics (two anterior, two posterior), with each spot labelled by its most enriched of five marker genes. ::: {.panel-tabset group="language"} ## R ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code code-fold="true" code-summary="Setup: download and label the data, define plotting helpers"} # Requires Seurat, hdf5r and ggplot2. library(Seurat) library(ggplot2) markers <- c("Mbp", "Slc17a7", "Penk", "Hpca", "Gabra6") ids <- c(anterior_1 = "V1_Mouse_Brain_Sagittal_Anterior", anterior_2 = "V1_Mouse_Brain_Sagittal_Anterior_Section_2", posterior_1 = "V1_Mouse_Brain_Sagittal_Posterior", posterior_2 = "V1_Mouse_Brain_Sagittal_Posterior_Section_2") cache <- tools::R_user_dir("friendlyspots", "cache") seurat_objects <- lapply(ids, function(id) { dir <- file.path(cache, id) if (!dir.exists(file.path(dir, "spatial"))) { url <- paste0("https://cf.10xgenomics.com/samples/spatial-exp/1.1.0/", id, "/", id) dir.create(dir, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE) download.file(paste0(url, "_filtered_feature_bc_matrix.h5"), file.path(dir, "filtered_feature_bc_matrix.h5")) download.file(paste0(url, "_spatial.tar.gz"), tar <- tempfile()) untar(tar, exdir = dir) } image <- Read10X_Image(file.path(dir, "spatial"), image.type = "VisiumV1") Load10X_Spatial(dir, image = image) }) labels <- lapply(seurat_objects, function(cells) { coords <- cells@images[[1]]@coordinates counts <- GetAssayData(cells, layer = "counts")[markers, rownames(coords)] counts <- as.matrix(counts) markers[max.col(t(counts / rowMeans(counts)), ties.method = "first")] }) plot_slices <- function(samples) { spots <- do.call(rbind, Map(cbind, sample = names(samples), samples)) ggplot(spots, aes(.data$array_col, -.data$array_row, color = .data$label)) + geom_point(size = 1.1, stroke = 0) + facet_wrap(~sample, nrow = 1) + coord_fixed(sqrt(3)) + scale_color_manual(values = c("#CC79A7", "#D55E00", "#0072B2", "#F0E442", "#009E73")) + guides(color = guide_legend(override.aes = list(size = 4))) + theme_void(base_size = 14) + theme(legend.position = "bottom", legend.title = element_blank()) } plot_similarity <- function(sim) { df <- as.data.frame(as.table(sim)) lower <- df[as.integer(df$Var1) >= as.integer(df$Var2), ] ggplot(lower, aes(.data$Var1, .data$Var2, fill = .data$Freq)) + geom_tile() + geom_text(aes(label = sprintf("%.2f", .data$Freq), color = .data$Freq < 0.1), size = 5, fontface = "bold", show.legend = FALSE) + scale_color_manual(values = c("black", "white")) + scale_fill_viridis_c(option = "inferno", name = "Similarity") + coord_fixed() + theme_minimal(base_size = 14) + theme(axis.title = element_blank(), axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1), text = element_text(face = "bold")) } ``` ::: Each sample is a data frame of spot array coordinates and labels: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} library(friendlyspots) samples <- Map(function(cells, label) { coords <- cells@images[[1]]@coordinates data.frame(array_row = coords$row, array_col = coords$col, label = label, row.names = rownames(coords)) }, seurat_objects, labels) head(samples$anterior_1) #> array_row array_col label #> AAACAAGTATCTCCCA-1 50 102 Mbp #> AAACACCAATAACTGC-1 59 19 Slc17a7 #> AAACAGAGCGACTCCT-1 14 94 Slc17a7 #> AAACAGCTTTCAGAAG-1 43 9 Mbp #> AAACAGGGTCTATATT-1 47 13 Penk #> AAACATGGTGAGAGGA-1 62 0 Slc17a7 ``` ::: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} plot_slices(samples) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](index_files/figure-html/r-slices-1.png) ::: ::: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} sim <- spatial_similarity(samples) round(sim, 2) #> anterior_1 anterior_2 posterior_1 posterior_2 #> anterior_1 1.00 0.93 0.00 0.01 #> anterior_2 0.93 1.00 0.03 0.04 #> posterior_1 0.00 0.03 1.00 0.92 #> posterior_2 0.01 0.04 0.92 1.00 plot_similarity(sim) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](index_files/figure-html/r-similarity-1.png){width=60%} ::: ::: ## Python ::: {.cell jupyter_compat='true'} ```{.python .cell-code code-fold="true" code-summary="Setup: download and label the data, define plotting helpers"} # Requires squidpy, matplotlib and seaborn. from pathlib import Path import matplotlib.pyplot as plt import numpy as np import seaborn as sns import squidpy as sq markers = ["Mbp", "Slc17a7", "Penk", "Hpca", "Gabra6"] ids = { "anterior_1": "V1_Mouse_Brain_Sagittal_Anterior", "anterior_2": "V1_Mouse_Brain_Sagittal_Anterior_Section_2", "posterior_1": "V1_Mouse_Brain_Sagittal_Posterior", "posterior_2": "V1_Mouse_Brain_Sagittal_Posterior_Section_2", } cache = Path.home() / ".cache" / "friendlyspots" adatas = {} labels = {} for name, sample_id in ids.items(): adata = sq.datasets.visium(sample_id, base_dir=cache) adata.var_names_make_unique() counts = adata[:, markers].X.toarray() top = (counts / counts.mean(axis=0)).argmax(axis=1) adatas[name] = adata labels[name] = np.array(markers)[top] def plot_slices(samples): palette = ["#CC79A7", "#D55E00", "#0072B2", "#F0E442", "#009E73"] colors = dict(zip(sorted(markers), palette)) fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, len(samples), layout="constrained") for ax, (name, df) in zip(axes, samples.items()): ax.scatter( df["array_col"], -df["array_row"] * np.sqrt(3), c=df["label"].map(colors), s=3, linewidths=0, ) ax.set_title(name) ax.set_aspect("equal") ax.axis("off") handles = [ plt.Line2D([], [], marker="o", linestyle="", color=color, label=label) for label, color in colors.items() ] fig.legend( handles=handles, loc="outside lower center", ncol=len(colors), frameon=False, ) plt.show() def plot_similarity(sim): style = {"font.size": 14, "font.weight": "bold", "figure.autolayout": True} with plt.rc_context(style): ax = sns.heatmap( sim, mask=np.tril(np.ones(sim.shape, dtype=bool), k=-1), annot=True, fmt=".2f", cmap="inferno", vmin=0, vmax=1, square=True, cbar_kws={"label": "Similarity"}, ) ax.invert_yaxis() plt.xticks(rotation=45, ha="right") plt.show() ``` ::: Each sample is a DataFrame of spot array coordinates and labels: ::: {.cell jupyter_compat='true'} ```{.python .cell-code} from friendlyspots import spatial_similarity samples = { name: adata.obs[["array_row", "array_col"]].assign(label=labels[name]) for name, adata in adatas.items() } print(samples["anterior_1"].head()) #> array_row array_col label #> AAACAAGTATCTCCCA-1 50 102 Mbp #> AAACACCAATAACTGC-1 59 19 Slc17a7 #> AAACAGAGCGACTCCT-1 14 94 Slc17a7 #> AAACAGCTTTCAGAAG-1 43 9 Mbp #> AAACAGGGTCTATATT-1 47 13 Penk ``` ::: ::: {.cell jupyter_compat='true'} ```{.python .cell-code} plot_slices(samples) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](index_files/figure-html/py-slices-1.png){width=960} ::: ::: ::: {.cell jupyter_compat='true'} ```{.python .cell-code} sim = spatial_similarity(samples) print(sim.round(2)) #> anterior_1 anterior_2 posterior_1 posterior_2 #> anterior_1 1.00 0.93 0.00 0.01 #> anterior_2 0.93 1.00 0.03 0.04 #> posterior_1 0.00 0.03 1.00 0.92 #> posterior_2 0.01 0.04 0.92 1.00 plot_similarity(sim) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](index_files/figure-html/py-similarity-3.png){width=60%} ::: ::: ::: The anterior sections are most similar to each other, as are the posterior sections, while anterior and posterior sections are dissimilar. ## Citation The algorithm and original implementation of `friendlyspots` are based on the methodology in: - Durkin _et al_. "Functional integration of an autologous engineered esophagus in a large-animal model." _Nature Biotechnology_ (2026). - Budinger _et al_. "An in vivo and in vitro spatiotemporal profile of human midbrain development." _Nature Communications_ (2026).
